description: CFM bond-head accuracy vs the corpus's TRUE bond graph (Wiberg bond orders read from tmQM .BO shards), scored pair by pair. This is the CFM bond-quality metric; it supersedes decode_ratio as the gate and as the reported number — see metrics/by_metric/decode_ratio.json ::blind_spot for why decode_ratio could not serve.
unit: ratio (0-1) over candidate pairs within the edge cutoff
scope: CFM (EGNN velocity field + YuelBond bond head) on tmQM
no_headline_reason: PROBE SCALE, deliberately unscalarised: this file reports the DIRECTION of each class-weight lever (precision/recall/F1/pr_auc per exponent) at 4 epochs on a 946-cloud cohort, and its own caveat states that exact-match and F1 at production scale are NOT yet measured. Picking one of those probe numbers as a headline would promote a lever-direction probe into an achievable-score claim. A scalar becomes declarable when the 20-epoch production run lands.

measured.cohort: tmQM real CSD-derived geometry, all six target metals (Pt/Ru/Ir/Rh/Os/Re), coord_number unfiltered, tmqm_val_frac 0.2, CSD-code-hash disjoint split
measured.caveat: PROBE SCALE. 4 epochs on a 946-cloud training cohort. The production config is 20 epochs; exact-match and F1 at production scale are NOT yet measured. These numbers establish the DIRECTION of each lever, not the achievable score.

class_weight_sweep.note: Inverse-frequency weighting on the bond cross-entropy, softened by an exponent. Counts measured on the training cohort: [24378, 4460, 421, 28, 5661] for [NO_BOND, SINGLE, DOUBLE, TRIPLE, AROMATIC]; weights are renormalised on sum_c(p_c * w_c) = 1 so the bond_ce loss keeps its scale in total = loss + ... at every exponent.
class_weight_sweep.verdict: power 0.5 is best on BOTH axes: highest argmax F1 (0.481) AND highest threshold-free PR-AUC (0.593). The textbook power 1.0 gives BOND_TRIPLE (0.08% of pairs, 28 examples) a 250x weight and is WORSE than no weighting at ranking (PR-AUC 0.467 vs 0.564) while saturating recall at 0.987 with precision 0.313 — it predicts a bond for nearly every pair. MEASURED, so the default is 0.5 and the 250x form is available but not used.

calibration.note: The decision rule matters as much as the weights. argmax over the 5 classes is the historical rule; a cut on P(bonded) is the alternative. The gap between the argmax F1 and the best F1 achievable by any P(bonded) cut, on the SAME logits:
calibration.verdict: sqrt weighting nearly closes the calibration gap (0.491 -> 0.089), so at power 0.5 the argmax operating point is close to optimal and threshold tuning buys little. Both rules are scored and printed every epoch (flow.bond_decision selects which drives the gate) so the choice stays measured rather than assumed.

honest_framing: MEASURED at probe scale (4 epochs, 946-cloud train cohort, 192 held-out clouds carrying 8,634 true bonds from tmQM's Wiberg .BO shards). What this ESTABLISHES: the objective and the metric are now correct (the target was previously synthesised by a Pt-only rule and was all-BOND_NO_BOND for every non-Pt metal), class weighting lifts recall as intended, and sqrt softening beats both no weighting and the textbook inverse frequency on both F1 and PR-AUC. What it does NOT establish: any achievable production score. bond_exact_match is 0.000 at every setting — no complex's full bond graph is reproduced — and PR-AUC 0.593 against a 0.299 base rate is a modest lift. The 20-epoch production run is required before any of this is quoted as a result. Not a wet-lab or experimental measurement of any kind.
